cues.text: Hello there. Do you work in the computer room?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Yes, I do. Can I help you?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Well, I’m a first year and I know that I’ll need to use the computer room for my work as I don’t have a computer of my own.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: So, I thought I’d get down here and see what I have to do in order to get time on one of the university's computers.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: OK. There are 4 computer labs open to undergraduates . The others can only be used by the staff and postgraduates .
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: The names of the 4 labs that you can use are Wimborne, Franklin, Salisbury and Court. wimborne and Court are in this building, the Johnson building, Franklin is in the Computer Sciences building and Salisbury is in the library.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: So I can use them whenever I like?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Well, you can use them but not whenever you like. As you can imagine they’re in quite a lot of demand so you have to reserve your time on a computer.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: In each of the labs there is a reservation book and you can reserve your time on a computer in that for 2 hours daily.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: If a computer is free though you can go on it straight away It’s quite straightforward but be sure to always write your name in the reservation book in pen or someone can rub it out and put their name in instead
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Oh my God! Does that really happen?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: I’m afraid so. And far more often than you would think. When people are stressed about their assignments they'd , they’ll do anything to get some time on the computers.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Better not try it yourself though or you’ll be banned from the computers for the rest of the academic year and your password and user name will be taken away.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: That reminds me. I’ve got to get a user name and password . How do I go about that then?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Well, what I’ll do is pass you over to my colleague , Jane, as she’s in charge of all that. Jane!
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Yes Dave.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I’ve got a new student here wanting to find out about user names and passwords. Can you help him out with that?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Yeah sure. Hi there.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Hi.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Well, it’s a straightforward process . First of all tell me your name and I’ll type it into the system.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: James Smith.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Right, let me do that. You see all students are automatically given a user name and then they just choose a password themselves .
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: OK. So, your user name is james smith - that’s all small case. That means there must be more than one of you at the university at the moment.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well, what do you want your password to be?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I think I’ll choose biology , as that’s the subject that I’m studying though my girlfriend Mary will be upset that it’s not her name I’m using.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Well, that’s all done. You can now use any of the four undergraduate computer labs.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: By the way, can I print out stuff at the labs?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Yes you can but sometimes it’s not quick. When you print it goes into a queue and it will be left in a tray in Franklin, as that’s where all the main printers are.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: The good bit is that, although last year it cost 3 pence per page,  now it doesn’t cost you anything.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I don’t really know much about computing. Is there any training available?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Yes. We have introductory courses for all new students. There is beginner, intermediate and advanced. Which would you like to go for?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Well, I have done some but I don’t know if I’m up to anything more than beginner. I’d better stick with that. intermediate could be too tough.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Well your course is in Franklin then. We’re in Court now. You know where that is?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: That’s in this building too, isn’t it?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: No that’s Wimborne you’re thinking about. Franklin’s over in the Computer Sciences Building. Anything else?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I don’t know what time the course starts.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Let’s have a look then. Advanced starts at 4:30 in the afternoon on Mondays but yours is the day after at 5 in the afternoon.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Are there any other times as I’ve got a part time job then.
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: Yes. You could try thursday at 2.00 pm. How’s that?
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: Even worse as I’ve a tutorial then. Anything else?
cues.speaker: Jim

cues.text: No. That’s it.
cues.speaker: Jane

cues.text: I’ll have to rearrange work then. I can’t miss the tutorial.
cues.speaker: Jim
